articles.title: 苹果库克：AI 应用正迎来爆发式增长，在多个方面对供应链产生深远影响
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据财联社报道，在今日举办的全球财富管理论坛 2026 上海苏河湾大会上，苹果公司执行董事长、清华大学经管学院顾问委员会主席蒂姆 · 库克（Tim Cook）指出，人工智能应用正迎来爆发式增长。当前，AI 辅助编程显著降低了编程门槛，使此前几乎未接触过代码的人群也能够编写代码。与此同时，人工智能已在多个方面对供应链产生深远影响。过去，质检环节高度依赖人工。如今，机器学习使检测变得高度自动化且更加精准。以 iPhone 颜色检测为例，为确保数百万台量产设备颜色保持一致，相关检测与成像工作均借助机器学习完成。据IT之家了解，这是库克卸任 CEO 转任董事会执行主席后首次访华，首站落地广州。随后库克现身清华大学，参加经管学院顾问委员会年会。库克还与商务部部长王文涛就中美经贸关系、人工智能发展、苹果公司在华业务等议题进行交流。库克表示，苹果公司看好中国发展前景，将进一步扩大在华业务，并愿为推动美中经贸关系稳定健康发展发挥积极作用。相关阅读：《广东省省长孟凡利会见苹果执行董事长库克一行，库克称愿意进一步扩大在粤业务布局》《苹果库克现身清华大学：参加经管学院顾问委员会年会，目前担任主席》《苹果库克、腾讯马化腾、百度李彦宏登上〈新闻联播〉，参加清华经管学院顾问委员会 2026 年会》《商务部部长王文涛会见美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克，就人工智能发展等进行交流》

articles.title: 江淮汽车涨停，工信部等三部门联合调查有关车辆刹车踏板支架断裂问题
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，今日早盘，汽车整车板块震荡反弹，江淮汽车涨停，北汽蓝谷、赛力斯、安凯客车、海马汽车、上汽集团跟涨。消息面上，针对网络反映的“尊界 V800 汽车刹车踏板支架断裂问题”，工业和信息化部、中央网信办、市场监管总局三部门 10 月 15 日晚宣布成立联合调查组开展核查，并依法依规处理。有关情况将及时公布。尊界汽车官方微博随后发布声明，表示将积极响应、完全服从并将全力配合联合调查组的工作。IT之家附声明原文如下：10 月 15 日，工信部等三部门发布了联合调查有关车辆刹车踏板支架断裂问题的通报。我们积极响应、完全服从并将全力配合联合调查组的工作，坚决维护消费者合法权益，坚决维护新能源汽车产业发展大局。

articles.title: “中子号”火箭首飞再推迟，火箭实验室股价应声大跌
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，美国商业航天公司火箭实验室（Rocket Lab）10 月 14 日宣布，推迟新一代可复用中型运载火箭“中子号”（Neutron）的首飞时间，由原定的 2026 年第四季度推迟至 2027 年。延期原因方面，火箭实验室首席执行官彼得 · 贝克（Peter Beck）表示，此次推迟主要源于火箭一级推进剂贮箱前部封头的制造问题。该部件为碳纤维复合材料结构，用于容纳推进剂，是火箭结构安全与飞行准备的关键环节。工程师在检测时发现了微小的空气孔隙或分层间隙，若强行发射可能引发严重的结构失效。这一消息打破了此前计划于 2026 年底首飞的预期，引发资本市场剧烈震荡。在延期消息公布前，火箭实验室股价已下跌约 7.9%；盘后再度走低。在消息发布后次日，股价一度下跌超过 14%，收盘下跌 6.6%，报 55.25 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 370.3 元人民币）。今年以来，该股累计下跌约 25%，较 5 月创下的 52 周高点 151 美元（现汇率约合 1,012 元人民币）回落约 65%。多家华尔街机构随后下调目标价，其中 KeyBanc 将其目标价由 135 美元（现汇率约合 904.9 元人民币）降至 100 美元（现汇率约合 670.3 元人民币），Clear Street 由 129 美元（现汇率约合 864.7 元人民币）降至 105 美元（现汇率约合 703.8 元人民币）。IT之家附上相关截图如下：

articles.title: 联想拯救者 R9 68 键磁轴电竞键盘开售：8KHz 轮询率，999 元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，联想拯救者 R9 68 键磁轴电竞键盘今日 10:00 正式开售，售价 999 元。这款键盘采用航空级铝合金外壳，采用阳极氧化 + 细腻喷砂工艺，可选拿铁磁轴 Pro 或紫璃磁轴 Pro；采用海王星 8K 电竞方案，可实现 0.001mm 高精度触发；拥有 8000Hz 硬件级轮询率，按键平均延迟约 0.1ms，最低可达 0.029ms。这款键盘内置 4 挡预设配置（日常、游戏、野兽、超能电竞），可通过 Fn+O 一键快速切换；支持多种高级按键功能，包含动态键程（DKS）、双效点击（MT）、多段触发（MPT）、松开触发（END）、火力开关（TGL）。这款键盘搭载 150 颗独立 ARGB 灯珠，三区独立光效；支持 LEGION Halo 联动光效模式，可实现键盘与拯救者笔记本、鼠标、耳机等全系设备灯效自动同步。IT之家附这款新品详细参数：京东联想拯救者 R9 68 键 磁轴电竞键盘 999 元直达链接

articles.title: 给大模型装上“一双耳朵”：小米开源空间音频理解大模型 MiDashengLM-Spatial
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，小米昨日宣布，带来 Dasheng 系列的重要新成员 ——MiDashengLM-Spatial，完整公开模型权重和推理代码，并以 Apache 2.0 许可证发布。过去两年，小米先后发布并开源了声音基座模型 Xiaomi Dasheng 及声音理解大模型 MiDashengLM-7B。相关技术已在小米智能家居、汽车座舱等场景实现超过 30 项落地应用，能够对语音、环境声音和音乐进行统一感知与理解。据介绍，新模型以 MiDashengLM-7B 为基座，进一步为声音理解大模型赋予“一双耳朵”，使其不仅能够听懂声音的内容，还能感知声音来自何处、如何在空间中分布。小米表示，MiDashengLM-Spatial 是业界首个开源的端到端空间音频理解大模型，在保留基础音频理解能力的同时，具备空间感知与推理能力，推动音频大模型从“听懂声音”进一步迈向“理解声音所处的空间”。该模型将陆续应用于小米智能家居、汽车座舱等场景，以空间听觉能力进一步提升“人车家全生态”的交互体验。相关测试数据如下：IT之家附相关链接：项目主页：https://jinbo-hu.github.io/midashenglm-spatial-demo/技术报告：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11156评估代码（GitHub）: https://github.com/xiaomi-research/midashenglm-spatial模型结构与权重（HuggingFace）：https://huggingface.co/mispeech/midashenglm-spatial

articles.title: 苹果首款智能家居中枢 HomeView 细节：同时显示九路监控、可当数码相框等
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，科技媒体 AppleInsider 昨日（10 月 15 日）发布博文，在发布会现场深入体验 HomeView 后，分享了关于苹果首款智能家居中枢的更多实用细节，包括九路监控、共享相册等。IT之家附上相关现场测试视频如下：安防方面，HomeView 的“Home Camera”界面可同时显示最多 9 路实时摄像头画面，用户无需逐一切换，就能查看房间、门口或室外区域。该媒体称在现场演示中，视频响应较快，也没有非常明显的延迟情况出现，不过实际家庭网络下的稳定性仍待验证。值得注意的是，尽管苹果新的 Home 系列配件普遍支持 Matter，不过智能家居安防摄像头暂时未采用 Matter 标准。苹果方面称，当前 Matter 相机规范在可靠性与安全性上仍有不足。HomeView 也试图承担“数码相框”的角色。它不仅可展示个人照片库，还支持 iCloud 共享相册：家人可以持续从 iPhone 添加照片，长辈或祖父母无需手动传输，屏幕便会自动更新。此外，“Flow”界面会借助摄像头感知附近移动并改变动画，而灵感来自日晷的“Fade”界面则会随时间调整时钟数字的明暗。在厨房场景中，用户可通过 Safari 或 Apple News 打开食谱，并以分步方式查看烹饪说明；Siri 支持语音跳转到下一步，食谱也可固定保存，方便日后调用。安装方面，壁挂版可搭配售价 79.95 美元的 Schneider Home Power Mount AC Wired 配件，通过标准单联墙盒直接接入家庭电路，经 USB-C 持续供电，从而隐藏线缆，甚至安装在原有灯开关位置。但苹果提醒，既有开关线路不一定适合供电，且需处理原照明回路，建议由持证电工安装。

articles.title: Meta 首席 AI 官汪滔：不会开源最强模型，但会继续发布优秀开源模型
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，当地时间 10 月 15 日，Meta 发布了开放权重 AI 模型 Muse Spark Open。Meta 官方宣称这是迄今为止能力最强的美国开放权重模型。据 The Next Web 报道，Meta 表示，Muse Spark Open 性能低于周一刚发布的前沿模型 Muse Wonder。Meta 曾在周一宣布 Muse Wonder 已达到前沿模型水准，但并未对外公布任何基准测试成绩，该模型目前依然保持闭源。Meta 首席 AI 官汪滔（Alexandr Wang）表示，出于安全与能力边界的双重考量，我们通常不会开源我们最顶尖的模型。不过他补充道，Meta 打算继续发布优秀的开源模型。据悉，这是 Meta 旗下 Muse 系列 AI 模型的第二次开源。今年 8 月，Meta 以 Apache 2.0 协议发布了从 Muse Spark 蒸馏而成的 300 亿参数模型 Glimmer。IT之家注意到，Meta 创始人五周前的言论与此截然相反。扎克伯格在 Sources 播客中表示，竞争对手训练出更先进的模型却不公开，是“极其危险”的行为（当时他并未具体点名任何企业）。相关阅读：《Meta 发布 Muse Wonder 系列旗舰 AI 模型，对标 Anthropic 与 OpenAI》《宣称“美国最强开源 AI 模型”：Meta 发布 Muse Spark Open》

articles.title: 元太发布 Kaleido 4 彩色电子纸，支持 18FPS 视频播放
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，元太科技 (E Ink) 昨日正式推出新一代彩色电子纸技术 E Ink Kaleido 4。该面板在延续低功耗、类纸阅读核心优势的同时，进一步提升彩色显示的色彩表现、亮度、对比度与动态显示能力。Kaleido 4 色域容积提升 2 倍至 40K 以上，白画面的反射率提升 15%，对比度提升 50%，更能清楚呈现图片、图表、简报与影音内容，减少画面颗粒感。其导入全新 Oxide TFT 背板，支持更高驱动电压，提升画面刷新速率；结合新算法，Kaleido 4 支持 18FPS 视频播放。同时，全新设计的前光系统让画面显色效果更加自然、清晰、细致。汉王科技率先基于该面板推出了 M10C 二代彩墨办公本。其翻页、滑动速度提升 27%，覆盖微蚀刻 AG 黑色钢化玻璃面板，搭配 8,192 级压感无源数位笔。该设备基于高通 8 核处理器，存储器组合为 4GB + 128GB。

articles.title: 这次能飞了！特斯拉第二代 Roadster 跑车正式亮相
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，在今天（16 日）上午的特别活动中，特斯拉第二代 Roadster 正式亮相，官方称其为“最后一辆最佳驾驶者之车”。根据介绍，2008 年的 Roadster 只有一个目标：证明电动汽车可以速度飞快、外形性感、引人期待，而今天发布的第二代 Roadster，则展现了历史上的一个新时刻：最后几辆人类驾驶汽车之中的佼佼者。新车配备姿态控制推进器和车尾主推进器，不仅能像火箭一样离地升空，还能在空中翻滚。据IT之家了解，第二代 Roadster 的核心亮点是搭载了特斯拉与 SpaceX 联合开发、内部代号 A71 的冷气推进系统。该套装置由多组高压气体喷嘴构成，无需燃料燃烧，可在极限工况下辅助强化加速表现、优化过弯能力，甚至有望实现车身短暂离地的设想。特斯拉为新车开发了一套风扇吸附系统，通过风扇产生的吸力将车身压向路面。特斯拉称，这套系统能够大幅提高抓地力，让 Roadster 过弯时的横向加速度最高达到 2g。特斯拉表示，Roadster 的过弯能力将强到令人觉得不可思议，仿佛违反了物理定律。公司还希望用新车打破赛道纪录，研发目标就是“突破现有跑车的性能极限”。发布会上，马斯克称，新车将于 2028 年开始生产。根据介绍，新车拥有主动式空气动力学系统、多模式吸附系统和冷气体推进器，是一款“真正的飞行员座驾”。其采用隐藏式前大灯、贯穿式尾灯和平整的车身表面，营造简约而富有科技感的造型。超轻量化轮圈采用纤细的辐条设计，同时确保车辆在地面行驶时的结构强度；Ano White 车漆采用源自航天领域的表面处理技术，具备抗紫外线、耐极低温、静电耗散和耐腐蚀性能。该车配备 Gold Glazed 有色玻璃，模仿宇航服面罩的镀铜涂层，并搭配低调的钛金属装饰。新车采用纯白色内饰，搭配灰色超细纤维麂皮装饰，座椅侧翼设计可增强对乘员身体的固定效果。同时，手动操控机构和固定式座椅设计有助于减轻整车重量。全车广泛采用镁、钛和碳纤维等轻质高强度材料，进一步降低车重。新车还拥有“突破物理极限”的配置：多模式风扇与车底密封系统通过抽走车底空气产生强大吸力，足以让车辆在静止状态下倒挂而不坠落。动力风扇与主动式扰流翼可在各种条件下最大限度提高抓地力和过弯速度，即使车辆静止，也能产生巨大的下压力。先进的冷气体推进器配合全电动执行机构，可在几分之一秒内完成细微调整，确保车辆在飞行过程中保持稳定。不同车型特性如下：Performance（性能版）：公路驾驶，双座，配备主动空气动力学系统和多模式风扇吸附系统，无论在公路还是赛道上，都能提供更出色的性能表现。Thrust（推进版）：赛道驾驶，双座，多模式风扇吸附系统搭配车尾冷气体推进器，0—97km/h 加速时间不到 1 秒。Rocket（火箭版）：飞行模式，单座，多模式风扇吸附系统搭配分布于车身周围的冷气体推进器，可实现向前、向上加速及横向旋转动作。该车续航里程超过 483km，Rocket 版的最高时速超过 370km/h，0-97km/h 加速时间如下：Performance：不到 1.6 秒Thrust：不到 0.9 秒Rocket：不到 0.59 秒

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，高通公司今日宣布，已与传音控股签订全球专利许可的长期续期，涵盖 4G 和 5G 移动设备，期限至 2031 年底。高通技术许可（QTL）执行副总裁兼总经理 John Han 表示：“我们很高兴能够提前续签传音控股的 4G 和 5G 许可证，并将现有的 4G 和 5G 协议合并为单一的长期协议。”IT之家注意到，高通近期密集与多家移动设备大厂签订了专利许可协议。9 月 24 日，高通宣布与苹果（Apple）续签全球专利许可协议，新协议将于 2027 年 4 月 1 日起生效。10 月 5 日，华为与高通宣布达成一项长期、广泛的专利许可协议，该协议包含双方在 5G、计算、人工智能、网络等多个技术领域的专利组合交叉许可，同时高通将收购华为在计算、人工智能、网络及其他技术领域的部分美国专利。高通公司旗下包括专利许可业务 QTL 以及绝大多数专利资产。高通公司旗下子公司高通技术公司及其子公司负责高通绝大部分工程和研发工作，以及几乎全部产品和服务业务，其中包括 QCT 半导体业务。

articles.title: 苹果 Minions 研究：闲置 Mac GPU 组队，几分钟就能完成 10 小时 AI 任务
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，科技媒体 AppleInsider 昨日（10 月 15 日）发布博文，报道称苹果研究团队公布了一项名为 Minions 的系统研究，尝试聚合闲置 Mac GPU，形成一个可动态调度的“虚拟 GPU 云”，用于运行大规模机器学习推理任务。IT之家援引博文介绍，传统 AI 推理通常依赖集中式 GPU 集群，面临成本高、扩容慢、排队时间长等问题；而 Mac 在日常办公、浏览和创作场景中，GPU 常常长期空闲。苹果公司在论文中阐述了 Minions 方案，希望重新组织这些“看不见的算力”，在不额外采购 GPU 的情况下，让多台 Mac 协同完成 AI 任务。根据论文概述，系统由四个关键部分组成：Minion Server 负责接收任务、拆分子任务并协调调度；PostgreSQL 元数据存储记录任务与设备状态；运行在各台 macOS 设备上的 Minion Executor 通过 Apple Silicon GPU 本地执行推理；Minion Watchdog 则监控设备掉线、休眠或断电等情况，并把未完成任务重新分配给其他可用设备。在技术实现上，Minions 采用“拉取式”任务模型：设备主动向服务器领取可执行的子任务，并通过原子化机制避免多台设备重复处理同一任务。推理结果可写入对象存储，系统还提供基于 Grafana 的实时监控面板，便于团队了解在线、忙碌和空闲设备数量。苹果披露的测试结果显示，此前因集中式 GPU 资源不足而需排队超过 10 小时的部分推理任务，在 Minions 下可在数分钟内开始执行；团队无需新增 GPU 硬件，也降低了基础设施成本。不过，这项技术目前更像是面向企业内部的研究与工程方案，而非面向普通消费者的正式产品。研究团队也指出，跨部门使用他人设备时，数据保密和治理是重要顾虑。参考Minions: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices

articles.title: 微软 Win11 照片应用史诗级重构：一站式管理本地 / iCloud 照片，编辑器加载提速 25%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，微软昨日（10 月 15 日）发布博文，宣布重构 Windows 11 系统自带“照片”（Photos）应用，并邀请 Windows Insider 项目成员测试，预估今年晚些时候面向所有 Windows 11 用户开放。界面方面，微软本次重新设计“图库”（Gallery）。用户无需来回切换多个应用，可以在同一个界面浏览本地电脑、OneDrive 以及 Apple iCloud 中的照片和视频。应用还支持按日期、人物、收藏等维度整理图片，并为 OneDrive 内容新增“Moments”功能，可自动将相关照片归类为回忆集，生成季节性回顾和幻灯片。搜索方面，用户不再需要记住文件名或拍摄时间，只需输入“海滩上的日落”等日常描述，即可查找对应照片。微软还提供人物筛选功能，用户可结合照片中的人物、存储位置等条件进一步缩小搜索范围。编辑方面，微软基于 WinUI 3 重建了照片编辑器，称启动速度较旧版提升约 25%。编辑工具被重新划分为裁剪、增强、修复和风格化四大板块。新版改进 AI 物体移除功能：用户只需涂抹或圈选画面中的多余人物、杂物，系统即可自动完成清理。IT之家附上相关动图如下：新增的“重新打光”（Relight）功能则允许用户在照片中添加最多三个虚拟光源，并调整光源颜色、亮度与方向。新版应用还增强了对 HDR、HEIC 和 WebP 等格式的支持，可在保留原始格式的情况下进行编辑和保存。图片查看器平均启动速度提升 15%，打开 HEIC 图片最快可提升 30%，并新增更清晰的 HDR 显示、SVG 支持以及包含相机参数、拍摄地点等信息的详情面板。

articles.title: 曝宁德时代乘用车业务换帅，将加快推进换电
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据 36 氪 10 月 15 日晚报道，宁德时代乘用车体系迎来重磅调整，宁德时代换电业务负责人、时代电服 CEO 杨峻将接替韩伟，兼任市场体系联席总裁，原市场体系联席总裁韩伟将回归商用车业务。报道称，国内乘用车业务副总裁王慧也随之调整。知情人士透露，王慧所负责业务将由宁德时代乘用车 CTO 高焕接棒，而王慧也同样回归商用车业务。报道认为，杨峻的接任，意味着宁德时代有望进一步打通乘用车电池销售与换电业务。过去几年，杨峻最重要的工作，就是推动宁德时代换电体系从技术方案走向商业化。据IT之家此前报道，在 2024 年底的巧克力换电生态大会上，宁德时代创始人、董事长、CEO 曾毓群表示，到 2030 年，换电、家充、公共充电桩将三分天下。今年 4 月，宁德时代正式发布巧克力 26#换电电池，其基于 800V 高压架构打造，首批上市产品为 75kWh 版本，未来还将提供更大电量，B 级车、C 级车都能用。“巧克力”“骐骥”（分别对应乘用车、重卡换电）换电站将全系标配神行超充桩，超换一体站方案带来 99 秒极速换电和更高效的超充体验。截至 9 月 29 日，巧克力换电全国累计建成换电站超 2520 座，站点落地覆盖 31 省 200 城，近 2 万块宁德品质全新电池完成入仓部署。根据规划，到 2026 年底，全国预计将建成超 3000 座巧克力换电站，覆盖近 216 座城市，在更多核心城区实现 10 分钟找站；2027 年预计将建成 1000 座高速换电站，形成“11 纵 9 横”全国高速换电骨干网络，远期目标布局 3 万座站点。

articles.title: 营收增长放缓，消息称投资者降低 Anthropic IPO 估值预期
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，北京时间今天（16 日）凌晨，路透社援引四名知情人士消息称，随着 AI 融资成本持续攀升引发市场担忧，Anthropic 公布最新财务数据后，部分现有投资者和准备参与 IPO 的投资者开始考虑下调对 Anthropic 的估值。其中三名知情人士称，部分投资者参加了 Anthropic 在旧金山举办的投资者日活动，并讨论了约 1.5 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 10.05 万亿元人民币）的估值。此前，投资者预计 Anthropic 在 11 月上市时的估值约为 2 万亿美元（现汇率约合 13.41 万亿元人民币）。Anthropic 向潜在投资者披露，第三季度营收达到 168 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,126.1 亿元人民币），环比增长 45%，并在调整部分财务项目后实现盈利。业绩数据缓解了部分投资者对 AI 研发成本高昂的担忧的同时，营收增速放缓仍令一些投资者失望。Anthropic 第二季度营收达到 116 亿美元（现汇率约合 777.55 亿元人民币），比第一季度增长一倍以上，第三季度的环比增幅则降至 45%。Anthropic 上市后的市场反响也可能影响整个 AI 行业的前景。投资者认为，短期内 AI 市场的表现很大程度上取决于 Anthropic 能否顺利上市，以及随后 OpenAI 能否在明年上市。投资者对 Anthropic 估值的顾虑，恰逢全球金融市场遭遇科技股抛售潮，AI 基础设施企业、芯片制造商，以及向 AI 企业出租算力的新兴云服务商均受到冲击。获得英伟达投资的 CoreWeave 周四股价和债券价格大跌，反映出市场越来越担忧 AI 基础设施建设对债务融资的依赖。如果 Anthropic 上市表现不佳，投资者对 AI 基础设施投资热潮的担忧可能进一步加深。此前消息称，Anthropic 在 2025 年的营收增至前一年的约 12 倍，接近 46 亿美元（现汇率约合 308.34 亿元人民币），但剔除主要由此前融资引起的负债减记影响后，经营亏损仍超过 80 亿美元（现汇率约合 536.24 亿元人民币）。Anthropic 的招股说明书提出，AI 对全球经济的影响将超过工业化、电力和互联网带来的变革。Anthropic 同时披露，2025 年亏损 420 亿美元（现汇率约合 2,815.25 亿元人民币），并预计未来建设 AI 基础设施还需要投入更多资金。

articles.title: The Investment Lessons Learned from 1873
articles.content: Long before the Great Depression or the 2008 financial crisis, the world endured its first truly global financial crash. In his new book, 1873: The Rothschilds, the First Great Depression, and the Making of the Modern World, Pulitzer Prize–winning author Liaquat Ahamed traces how a booming global bond market, railroad speculation and massive flows of capital helped fuel extraordinary growth before the bubble burst. At the center of the story were the Rothschilds, the powerful banking dynasty that helped transform government borrowing and global finance. Ahamed joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss why 1873 still matters, how railroad mania compares with today’s rush into AI infrastructure, and what the era can teach investors about bubbles, monetary-policy mistakes and financial resilience. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Qwen-Audio-Jev: A Unified Interface for Audio Decisions
articles.content: Large audio language models (LALMs) have made substantial progress in audio understanding. However, in high-throughput applications requiring frequent selection, judgment, and scoring, autoregressive text generation introduces additional computational overhead and response latency. To address this limitation, we introduce Qwen-Audio-Jev by augmenting Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next with a dedicated Jev decision head. The model unifies selection, binary judgment, and scoring through three decision primitives: CHOICE, NOUL, and SCORE. Given audio, a natural-language question, and an explicit answer specification, it directly produces a task-conditioned probability distribution or a numerical score through typed decision readouts. Evaluation across 18 labeled configurations covers all three primitives: for CHOICE, Qwen-Audio-Jev achieves accuracies of 78.70% on MMAU-mini and 84.06% on MMSU; for NOUL, it achieves an equal error rate of 6.50% on the VoxCeleb1-O speaker verification benchmark; and for SCORE, the model achieves a normalized mean absolute error of 0.1062 on NISQA overall quality assessment, with Pearson and Spearman correlations of 0.8210 and 0.8074, respectively. Compared with the original Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next, Qwen-Audio-Jev achieves an approximately 20x inference speedup. It demonstrates its potential for efficient, high-throughput audio decision-making in applications such as large-scale audio screening, speaker verification, and automated quality assessment.

articles.title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models
articles.content: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. We investigate the connection between action predictability, defined as the ability to reconstruct an action from consecutive latent states, and the preservation of intrinsic dynamics. Our central hypothesis is that encouraging action predictability discourages representations from discarding the distinctions between different actions and their consequences. We provide two complementary forms of evidence for this connection. Theoretically, we derive a positive lower bound on squared inverse prediction error when the encoder merges distinguishable outcomes of different actions from the same state and appearance, and show that forward prediction can still be exact on those transitions. Empirically, controlled appearance-diversity comparisons, supervision interventions, and latent probes support the role of action prediction in preserving control-relevant transition information. We instantiate action predictability with Concat IDM, which predicts actions from concatenated latent states and updates the shared encoder using action labels already available in offline trajectories, without changing the test-time planner. Across three independent training runs on Push-T with 24 appearances, Concat IDM increases planning success from 9.1% to 77.2%; its paired improvement is 52.9 percentage points larger than that observed with a single appearance. Together, these findings support action predictability as an inductive bias toward intrinsic dynamics and demonstrate the practical benefits of Concat IDM for latent planning under visual diversity.

articles.title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment
articles.content: Despite their practical significance, modern AI systems pose significant societal risks, including toxicity, malicious use, and misinformation. Their mitigation depends not only on technical feasibility but also on the incentives of firms that develop and deploy these systems. We show how profit maximization shapes safety investment in an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and several competing downstream firms. In our game-theoretic model, we derive the market-driven level of safety investment and compare it with the levels that maximize market welfare and industry profit. We find that downstream competition generally induces downstream firms to invest more in safety than the industry-profit-optimal level. By contrast, the upstream provider may underinvest relative to these benchmarks because it is not fully compensated for the surplus from safety investments. Finally, we analyze how different regulatory interventions affect the participants' incentives and profits, and the resulting levels of model safety.

articles.title: Evaluating Inquiry Learning in LLM-Based Agents: Hypothesizing, Reasoning, and Exploration
articles.content: Scientific inquiry involves iterative cycles of exploration, hypothesis generation, and reasoning over observations to uncover relationships in complex systems. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in several components of this process, including inductive reasoning, hypothesis generation, and data analysis. However, prior work typically evaluates these abilities in isolation, leaving open how models integrate them across a full inquiry cycle. In this work, we introduce a framework for evaluating LLMs' inquiry capabilities in a unified, interactive setting. We extend the Countdown task to a mathematical environment where an agent probes the system by manipulating variables, collecting observations, and inferring relationships between them. This setup enables analysis of exploration strategies, causal discovery, and hypothesis refinement during inquiry. Across seven LLMs and multiple prompting strategies, our experiments reveal limited inherent inquiry capabilities and low success rates in discovering the underlying expressions. However, structured guidance inspired by educational scaffolding significantly improves performance. Our findings highlight current limitations of LLMs in strategic exploration and iterative hypothesis refinement, and show how simple guidance strategies developed for human learners in inquiry learning can support more effective inquiry behavior.

articles.title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation
articles.content: Policy-shift distillation reuses the difference between a teacher's log probabilities before and after reinforcement learning (RL) as supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, this endpoint policy shift cannot reveal whether local action preferences evolved consistently during teacher training. The same endpoint shift can result from early and late shifts that reinforce or partially cancel each other. We investigate whether agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts can guide selective transfer. We introduce Waypoint-guided On-Policy Distillation (Waypoint-OPD), which uses an intermediate teacher checkpoint from the same RL run to compare early and late shifts in relative action preferences at student-visited prefixes. We gate the endpoint shift according to the directional agreement between the early and late shifts, suppressing it when they point in opposing directions. Compared with endpoint-only transfer, our method requires only one additional frozen-teacher scoring pass. Using RL-trained Qwen3-4B teachers, we evaluate our method with Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B as student models in mathematical and code reasoning. In all six domain--student settings, Waypoint-OPD achieves the highest domain-average score among the compared distillation methods. Ablations with the Qwen3-8B student show that removing or shuffling gates reduces mathematical reasoning performance. These results support the use of directional agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts to weight the endpoint shift during student training.

articles.title: Decoding What iOS Location Services Send to Apple: An LLM Is an Unreliable Analyst but a Useful Toolmaker
articles.content: Reverse engineering the data formats used by mobile software is skilled and slow, and using AI to assist with it is attractive. We evaluate this for the protobuf messages that an iPhone sends to Apple's location services. Working from Apple's binaries, we use two frontier models (Claude Opus 4.8, Codex GPT Sol 5.6) to reconstruct the schemas of protobufs observed in network traffic. The great majority of the schemas contain substantial errors, and these are hard to detect because the schemas are internally consistent. Direct AI use is therefore unsuitable for forensic and privacy analysis. AI can, however, write reliable analysis tools when their output can be validated. We use Claude to write a Python tool, Extractor, that reliably recovers protobuf schemas from Apple binaries. We validate it against binaries compiled from schemas with known answers, previously published schemas, and network measurements. We demonstrate the use of Extractor to decode and analyse the location services network traffic of a jailbroken iPhone 8 (iOS 16.7.11).

articles.title: LoopAhead: Speculating Ahead for Faster Decoding in Looped Language Models
articles.content: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by repeatedly applying the same Transformer layers. However, generating each token still involves sequential computation and repeated access to model weights, leading to high decoding latency. Recent pipelined self-speculative decoding methods reduce this delay by drafting tokens from early-loop predictions and asynchronously advancing tokens at different recurrent depths in the same batch, but they do not fully exploit early-loop features for longer lookahead and still spend computation verifying incorrect speculative branches. We introduce \method, a speculative decoding framework for looped transformers that enables earlier drafting of future tokens and assigns complementary roles to different recurrent depths. A lightweight lookahead drafter (LAD) predicts multiple future tokens with early-loop states, and deeper-loop feedback helps decide which draft branches to continue and which to pause, while the full-depth model makes the final token decisions. LoopAhead achieves up to 7.82x decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding while preserving the target model's output distribution.

articles.title: LOADBench: A Large Open Analog Dataset and Benchmark for Machine Learning in IC Design
articles.content: Machine learning (ML) for analog IC design is constrained by limited open data and the absence of standardized evaluation: results reported in different papers are typically obtained on bespoke, often closed, datasets and with ad-hoc metrics, leaving comparisons across methods unreliable. We address both gaps with a large opensource dataset and a suite of standardized benchmarks. The dataset contains more than 100 operational amplifier (opamp) topologies (1-, 2-, and 3-stage) in the SkyWater130 PDK, each shipped with structural and functional annotations, topology-specific sizing constraints (symmetry and sizing rules), an Ngspice testbench, and a multi-objective NSGA-II sizing run producing around 103 Pareto-optimal and 106 intermediate sizing-performance pairs per topology. On top of this data we define six benchmark tasks with precise protocols: inverse sizing, topology selection, sub-circuit classification, structural circuit generation, Pareto-membership prediction, and multi-objective optimization. Thus, the data presented here constitutes the most comprehensive dataset for ML development in over four decades of analog IC design automation. The dataset, ground-truth annotations, and reference implementations of the metric-defining routines are released under an open license, enabling reproducible and directly comparable evaluation across heterogeneous analog design automation methods.

articles.title: A Flow-Theoretic Multimodal Control Framework Fusing Mental and Physical Engagement for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation
articles.content: While Assist-as-Needed (AAN) control aims to maximize user participation in robot-assisted training, existing methods relying solely on physical metrics cannot distinguish muscular inability from mental disengagement, leading to suboptimal interventions. To address this ambiguity, a Flow-theoretic multimodal AAN framework is proposed, fusing EEG-based mental engagement and sEMG-based physical engagement into an adaptive impedance control strategy. A four-quadrant fuzzy decision engine translates these dual physiological metrics into continuous control policies. This enables the upper-limb exoskeleton to inject feedforward assistance during intent-execution mismatch (e.g., motor output attenuation despite mental focus) and escalate guiding stiffness to penalize mental distraction. The framework was validated with healthy participants against a state-of-practice sEMG-only AAN baseline. Kinematically and mechanically, the proposed framework reduced robotic energy expenditure by 71.9\% while maintaining precise trajectory tracking, confirming it elicited greater voluntary human effort. Physiologically, the system increased the time spent in the neuroplasticity zone (Flow State Ratio) from 4.6% to 42.8%. These results validate that decoupling and jointly regulating mental and physical states enhances the selectivity of robotic assistance, mitigating user passivity and sustaining the engagement crucial for motor learning.

articles.title: Hear, Localize, and Reason: Spatially Aware Scene Understanding for Audio-Visual LLMs
articles.content: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) have made strong progress in multimodal understanding, yet most treat audio as monaural semantic content, limiting their ability to reason about where sounds originate and how they relate to the visual scene. Recent spatial audio-visual studies address parts of this problem, but often focus on specific abilities, such as spatial correspondence or direction and distance reasoning. In this work, we introduce HLR-AVSceneQA, a comprehensive benchmark with a hear-localize-reason hierarchy that evaluates whether models can recognize what is heard, localize sound sources in egocentric and allocentric views, and use these localized sources to reason about how they relate to the visual scene. We further introduce HLR-LLM, which augments a strong audio-visual foundation model with a binaural spatial audio branch alongside its monaural semantic audio pathway. We train HLR-LLM with a curriculum that incorporates final-stage chain-of-thought supervision for multi-step spatial reasoning. Experiments show that existing AV-LLMs remain limited in spatial grounding and relational reasoning, while HLR-LLM substantially improves spatial audio-visual scene understanding without compromising semantic audio-visual perception.

articles.title: AVALON: Zero-Shot Indoor Navigation with Human-Seeded Topological Memory
articles.content: Indoor service robots often enter unmapped buildings whose layouts and task constraints are already familiar to users. We address this human-familiar, robot-unseen setting with AVALON, a topological navigation framework organized around human-seeded layered spatial memory, node-verified topological execution, and task-triggered, evidence-gated human--robot memory co-updating. The robot has no prior on-site traversal or site-specific training. Deployment requires only a floor plan, place clues, and an initial topology-odometry alignment. Visual depth point-goal navigation leverages verified node arrivals to perform translational re-anchoring, without requiring a robot-constructed global SLAM map. Human--robot memory co-updating fuses complementary sources of information. Human operators specify task constraints that are unobservable via vision and report offline environmental modifications, whereas the robot provides physical-state evidence through active in-situ validation. Task relevance governs whether human-reported environmental changes undergo robot validation during the active mission. Field-collected perceptual evidence gates memory updates, maintaining an explicit separation between human-specified permissions and robot-observed traversability. Our experiments on a Unitree Go2 show that AVALON with X-NavDP completes a 12.81 m Intersection-to-Dining mission in 46.4 s (5/5) with no mapping, 40.9% less robot time than DimOS-Go2 (78.5 s, 4/5), while policy-only X-NavDP times out in all of the 5 runs. These demonstrate the superiority of the proposed topological navigation framework.

articles.title: Transfer Learning in Bandits from Unknown Adaptive Policies: Problem-Dependent Lower and Upper Bounds
articles.content: Transfer learning in stochastic multi-armed bandits is typically studied assuming that prior data forms a fixed offline dataset or is generated by a known source. In practice, historical observations come from a previous adaptive decision process whose policy is unknown. We study this setting for bounded rewards in $[0,1]$.   Before the online game starts, the learner receives, for each arm $k$, $N'_k$ observations drawn i.i.d.\ from an unknown distribution $ν'_k$, collected by an arbitrary and possibly data-dependent strategy, so the sample sizes $N'_k$ may be random. Source and target means satisfy $|μ_k-μ'_k|<L_k$ for known constants $(L_k)_k$.   We derive an asymptotic problem-dependent lower bound and propose KL-UCB-Transfer, which combines online and historical data and achieves logarithmic regret with an improved leading constant whenever $μ'_a<μ_1-L_a$, and recovers the classical KL-UCB guarantee otherwise. Since bounding the source-target discrepancy is often unrealistic, we relax the assumption to the one-sided condition $μ_k-μ'_k<L_k$ and show that logarithmic regret can survive under misspecification, characterizing three regimes ranging from improvement to a degraded logarithmic bound to a loss of guarantee. Simulations illustrate the practical benefits of exploiting process-generated historical data.

articles.title: ClaimScope: Label-Blind Witness Verification for Mathematical Claim Auditing
articles.content: Mathematical agents are commonly evaluated by answer accuracy or proof acceptance. We introduce ClaimScope, a 72-task benchmark for auditing proposed claims through a verdict, scope, counterexample, and repair. Tasks cover optimizer-state transport, finite-horizon affine recurrences, and exact $2\times2$ linear algebra. We evaluate Qwen3-8B with direct generation and four matched two-pass conditions, each starting from the same draft. A witness checker evaluates only the model's submitted state, without consulting reference verdicts or supplying a replacement witness. Its feedback still conveys information about validity: a verified refutation establishes that the claim is false, and rejection reasons can suggest structural fixes. In this evaluation, verifier feedback yields $23/39$ accepted counterexamples on invalid claims and $25/72$ safe completions, compared with $15/39$ and $20/72$ for checker-free generic feedback. Strict completion remains $17/72$; verdict accuracy changes from $47/72$ to $46/72$. The claim-grouped safe-completion difference is $.094$, with a bootstrap 95\% interval of $[.000,.198]$. All seven task-level gains follow horizon/input-length diagnostics. A post-hoc schema-only correction of the direct outputs reaches the same 25 safe tasks without another model call. These results separate claim classification from executable evidence, while locating the observed gains in witness-structure correction rather than demonstrating broader reasoning improvement.

articles.title: Learning to Search for Executable Patternmaking from Certified Programs
articles.content: Recent models generate sewing patterns from images or text, and program-based representations make these patterns executable. These systems produce a finished pattern and do not model how a patternmaker turns one pattern into another. In practice a new style is made by editing an existing pattern: lengthening the bodice, moving a dart, swapping a sleeve. Pattern archives record the results of such edits and none of the steps. We observe that the steps can be recovered by searching over editing actions until one pattern becomes the other. A deterministic compiler makes the recovered steps checkable. To this end, we present SemDraft, the first framework that learns to search for executable patternmaking programs from paired before-and-after sewing patterns without recorded editing steps. Specifically, a bounded search recovers a program of editing actions and certifies it only after three checks: it recompiles from scratch, every pair of its actions is classified as ordered or interchangeable, and an independent replay reaches the same pattern. The certified programs then train a model that ranks candidate actions inside the same search. On two frozen draws of 80 order-sensitive cases, with every other search component fixed, the learned ranker certifies 63 and 64 cases within 1,000 search executions, against at most 53 and 52 for non-learned rankers.

articles.title: MYOPIA: Understanding the Limits of Tree-Based Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Decision trees can make vision-language model (VLM) classification interpretable by replacing a single prediction with a sequence of root-to-leaf questions. However, the accuracy cost of this greedy, non-backtracking procedure remains unclear. We introduce \textbf{MYOPIA}, a benchmark comprising four LLM-generated, human-refined decision trees for GTSRB, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MSCOCO, together with matched prompts, diagnostic protocols, and an evaluation harness. Across GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA-3.2 11B Vision, tree traversal underperforms zero-shot prompting in all 12 dataset--model pairs; paired bootstrap analyses consistently favor zero-shot. Our diagnostics characterize interacting failure modes associated with this gap. Models often recall tree-encoded class attributes more accurately than they ground the same attributes in images: the mean label--image accuracy gaps are 9.5, 13.8, and 12.6 points for GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA, respectively. Incorrect local decisions then irreversibly exclude the correct class, while answer extraction introduces additional model-dependent loss. A node-level audit of the four trees finds that split entropy is weakly but consistently associated with lower node accuracy, whereas depth, branching factor, and within-node grounding differences are less stable. \textbf{MYOPIA} therefore provides a framework for diagnosing hierarchical visual classification and motivates testing tree designs that prioritize perceptual answerability and recovery from early errors. Code is available at https://github.com/islammesabah/VLM_Classification.

articles.title: Rethinking the Role of Tool Graph Memory in Multi-Turn Tool Use
articles.content: Large language model (LLM) agents solve complex tasks by calling external tools over multiple turns. Recent work has proposed tool graph memory, which stores past experience as tool transitions to guide subsequent selection. However, it remains unclear whether this component consistently improves agents' tool use or undermines it. We evaluate tool graph memory on nine models and two benchmarks, finding that it seldom improves significantly over baselines, and that its gains, where present, cost over twice the LLM calls. The memory's guidance is often incorrect, and random or no guidance retains most of the gain, implying that the benefit stems from extra computation rather than the memory itself. Moreover, even with the correct next tool suggested, many failures remain, such as giving up without a tool call. Storing the same experience instead as textual insights outperforms tool graph memory with almost no extra LLM calls. This suggests that memory serves better as a soft prior than as a prescription of the next tool, leading to a more effective and generalizable solution.

articles.title: Independent Data-Integrity Verification for LLM-Driven Functional Coverage Closure in Hardware Design
articles.content: LLM agents can write directed tests that close functional coverage, but coverage only shows that a state was reached, not that the data on the way there was correct. This is a long-known point in verification and we do not claim it as new. We describe a small coverage-closure agent that applies it to an LLM loop: coverage is read from the report that the simulation itself exports (cocotb-coverage YAML) and never taken from the model's account, and data integrity is checked by scoreboards that are separate from the model. On three architecturally distinct RTL designs (an asynchronous FIFO, a UART transmitter and an AHB2APB bridge) the agent raised coverage from 91.7%, 88.9% and 67.4% to 100% within its 8-iteration budget in every logged run, using one design-agnostic agent. A reactive scoreboard monitor attached to the FIFO's base testbench also found a clock-domain-crossing bug in the author's own stimulus code. The monitor is not yet attached to the LLM-generated tests, so their data integrity is not independently checked; one manual check on a single FIFO test is reported as preliminary. We list the weaknesses of this evidence: three designs, no baseline, no ablation, and logged runs that come from several agent checkpoints.

articles.title: Decoupled Safety Control: A Safety-Control Algorithm for Training-Free Safety Guidance
articles.content: Diffusion models achieve strong performance in text-to-image generation, but they can still produce unsafe content. Training-free safety guidance offers a practical inference-time alternative that intervenes during sampling without modifying model weights. However, many existing safeguards still rely on a coupled safety-control chain. In this chain, the same unsafe condition simultaneously specifies what should be avoided, indicates the current unsafe signal, constructs the intervention, and determines when that intervention remains active. This coupling can work when unsafe factors are explicit, but becomes less reliable once harmful and benign semantics are entangled in the current generation state, often leaving residual unsafe content or unnecessarily degrading benign-generation quality or prompt fidelity. We address this problem with Decoupled Safety Control (DSC), a plug-in safety-control algorithm for training-free safety guidance. DSC reformulates training-free safety guidance as an explicit state-dependent control process, so the executed intervention is determined from the current generation state rather than inherited directly from a single unsafe condition. Experiments on standard safety benchmarks show that DSC improves representative latent- and text-space safeguards, achieving stronger unsafe-content suppression while preserving benign-generation quality and maintaining efficient inference.

articles.title: From Perception to Prediction and Intervention: Benchmarking Proactive Video Assistants in Real-Life Scenarios
articles.content: Recent multimodal large language models have advanced video understanding, but existing benchmarks mainly evaluate whether models can interpret observed visual content. In real-world scenarios, assistants must additionally anticipate what assistance is needed and decide when to provide it. To address this gap, we introduce \textsc{P$^3$IBench}, a benchmark for proactive video understanding in real-life streaming scenarios. It evaluates three complementary capabilities: daily perception, risk prediction and intervention. We benchmark 12 representative open-source and proprietary video-language models, including streaming and adapted non-streaming systems. Our evaluation shows that current models struggle to make well-calibrated response decisions. Finally, we construct additional proactive training data and train \textsc{P$^3$I-Assistant-4B}, achieving improvements on several tasks, though gains remain uneven across capabilities. Together, these findings show that effective proactive assistance requires not only visual understanding, but also precise response timing and appropriate restraint.

articles.title: Sharp and Stable Label-Free Calibration Certificates from Logical Coherence
articles.content: Query-conditioned probabilistic predictors answer logically related questions one at a time, and labels to check their calibration are often missing. For each restriction on what a bettor's stakes may use, a minimax theorem identifies, for finitely supported laws of the answers, the sharp label-free lower bound on the corresponding calibration residual. On bundles of different events its mean, marginal and joint stages can separate strictly, and a bundle's bound cannot be attributed to one question without assumptions on the others. The sharp marginal bound is discontinuous in the answers, and no label-free lower bound continuous in the Wasserstein distance stays within a constant factor of it. Lipschitz stakes give a stable bound, sharp for a smooth calibration residual and, for every positive Lipschitz constant, positive exactly when the sharp marginal bound is. On i.i.d. streams, projected online gradient ascent at fixed nodes gives fixed-horizon certificates whose shortfall is bounded by grid, learning and statistical terms, and predictable betting gives anytime-valid ones. In a preregistered study of four predictors on two data sets, all seven confirmatory certificates were positive (the eighth pair did not pass the pilot). A certificate shows only that calibration is at least this bad; zero means "not refuted".

articles.title: BiShield-TEE: On the (In-)Security of Unilateral Weight Obfuscation in On-Device TEE-Shielded LLM Partition
articles.content: On-device deployment of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly adopted due to latency and privacy requirements, but exposes proprietary models to reverse engineering and intellectual property theft. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) provide hardware-enforced isolation for on-device inference, yet most TEE-based parameter obfuscation relies on unilateral matrix transformations that obfuscate only output side. We identify a vulnerability in this design, termed the \emph{Solution Determinacy Property (SDP)}: the obfuscation secret is uniquely determined, exposing the structure of the true key and enabling attackers to break the protection. Under our attacks, representative methods \textsc{GroupCover} and \textsc{ArrowCloak} are reduced to negligible protection, with attack accuracy reaching over $2.4\times$ the full-shielding black-box baseline and recovering near-complete model functionality.To address this vulnerability, we propose \textsc{BiShield-TEE}, a bilateral framework that induces \emph{Ambiguous Solutions} through joint obfuscation of input and output dimensions, hiding the true key among many equally valid candidates. Experiments across diverse models and datasets show that \textsc{BiShield-TEE} confines attack accuracy to the full-shielding black-box baseline, while achieving higher inference efficiency than prior methods on real hardware.Our code is available at https://github.com/laduiw/BiShield-TEE.

articles.title: A Quantum Machine Learning Approach to Content-Based Media Recommendation
articles.content: We use quantum machine learning techniques to develop a content-based media recommender system and evaluate its performance on TV programmes using textual descriptions from one week of BBC iPlayer data. Grounded in the Quantum Natural Language Processing framework (QNLP), programme synopses are mapped to variational quantum circuits using their semantic structure. The parameters of these circuits are trained via a supervised pairwise similarity learning task.   We benchmark the quantum recommender against a classical BiLSTM baseline trained on the same dataset and objective. While both models achieve comparable performance on the similarity learning task, the quantum model requires significantly fewer parameters (47k vs. 17.8M). When the BiLSTM is constrained to a matching parameter budget, its performance degrades substantially (by 3.63 percentage points in Mean Average Precision (MAP)), indicating that the structured quantum representation provides a highly parameter-efficient alternative in this setting. We demonstrate the feasibility of executing the trained models on quantum hardware by deploying the circuits on Quantinuum's System Model H2 (and accompanying emulator) using a SWAP-test-based protocol. The results confirm that the similarity signal is preserved under realistic, noisy conditions. Taken together, these findings highlight the potential of variational quantum circuits for recommendation tasks and represent a practical step toward their real-world deployment.

articles.title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents
articles.content: Large language models (LLMs) deployed as conversational agents are increasingly expected to follow procedural logic. While factual hallucination has received extensive attention, a different failure mode has been overlooked: procedural hallucination, in which an agent produces individually fluent and factually plausible utterances while deviating from the intended conversational process. We introduce DialFork, the first benchmark to measure this failure mode on raw dialogue text. DialFork is built by forking conformant dialogues at controlled turn positions and injecting one of four hallucination types, yielding 36,278 dialogues across 24 tasks in 12 domains; 30 human annotators validate the construction. We define three evaluation tasks that characterize procedural deviation at three granularities: how far a set of dialogues deviates from conformant ones (monitoring deployed agents), how far a single dialogue does (procedural retrieval), and at which turn a dialogue first goes off-track (real-time guardrails). For the first two, we propose dialog-flow-aware metrics, FlowKL and FlowScore, that compare dialogues by how they unfold rather than their content. At the dialogue level, FlowScore significantly outperforms all baselines across seven encoders, showing that semantic similarity is no substitute for procedural similarity. We release DialFork under the MIT license at https://github.com/idiap/dialfork, hoping the community will measure conversational process alongside content.

articles.title: Reducing the Cost of Qudit State Preparation by Learning a Sparse Structure for SNAP Gates
articles.content: Preparing quantum states in bosonic qudits with SNAP--Displacement sequences requires both optimizing the gate parameters and deciding which Fock levels should be controlled by each SNAP gate. A fully parameterized ansatz assigns an independent phase to every Fock level in every gate, leading to a number of phases that grows steeply. This constitutes a problem for short to medium term systems as controlling many phases requires complex control pulses which are subject to increased control errors. Previous work reduced this cost by restricting the trainable phases to predefined sparse patterns, such as a diagonal or a grid, which however may not be optimal for a specific target state. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a method that learns which phases are needed together with their values, using a differentiable mask. A sparsity penalty encourages the removal of unnecessary phases, while temperature annealing gradually turns the masks into binary decisions. We compare the proposed method with fully parameterized and predefined sparse ansatzes on Fourier and Haar-random target states. The evaluation considers both the minimum number of phases required to reach different infidelity thresholds and the overall trade-off between fidelity and phases required, measured through Pareto frontiers and hypervolume. The results show that learning the location of the phases together with their values provides competitive or improved fidelity--resource trade-offs, although the advantage depends on the target state and qudit dimension.

articles.title: When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark
articles.content: Muon's gains in data efficiency motivate evaluating its performance under explicit data, time, and tuning budgets. On a single A100 GPU, we compare a reference single-device Muon implementation with AdamW across 17.7M- and 33.6M-parameter causal language models and 2.70M-parameter vision transformers. A common 23-candidate development budget selects configurations evaluated with five matched seeds, full validation trajectories, optimizer-step timing, and a frozen one-shot test. Muon reduces validation-loss area under the curve by 3.25--22.44\% at equal data and lowers test loss in all 20 primary pairs. In this configuration, Muon improves time-normalized loss area} by 19.68--22.31\% on vision, while AdamW is better by 3.38--6.96\% on language. The full Muon optimizer call, including auxiliary AdamW updates, consumes 56.1--69.6\% of training time, compared with 6.1--9.1\% for the AdamW baseline. Muon also has higher expected regret under restricted access to these candidate pools. These results characterize small models with reference kernels; their wall-clock ordering does not establish a ranking for larger models or optimized implementations.

articles.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification
articles.content: Instead of learning a mapping from instances to outcomes in the standard way, the key idea of pairwise difference learning (PDL) is to learn a function that takes two instances as input and predicts the difference between the respective outcomes. Given a function of this kind, predictions for a query instance are derived from every training example and then averaged. We propose a version of PDL for the task of classification and propose a suitable meta-learning technique for this purpose. Moreover, we address the problem of uncertainty quantification, i.e., of representing and quantifying the uncertainty of a PDL classifier's predictions in a faithful manner. Building on recent work on the decomposition of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components, we propose different ways of extending corresponding measures to the setting of PDL, depending on how and to what extent uncertainty is represented by the underlying base learner. In large-scale empirical studies, we analyze both the predictive accuracy and the uncertainty awareness of our PDL classifier.

articles.title: Writability and the Pathway: A Controlled Study of Knowledge Injection into Addressed Memory
articles.content: Addressed conditional memory provides a local surface for post-hoc knowledge injection, but a successful write need not transfer to a new question or preserve untargeted behavior. This study combines a controlled GPT-2 comparison with production-memory experiments on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Newly initialized modules attached to frozen GPT-2 are tested in a 2 x 2 design: row-only versus row-plus-projection updates, each with or without fixed module-residual anchoring. All arms reproduce 50 trained completions in each of three sampling seeds. Natural-question target-string hits average 5.3% for both row-only arms, 28.7% for unanchored projection updates, and 22.0% with anchoring, while strict answer scores remain zero. Anchoring lowers measured drift; lexical hits do not establish entity-specific retrieval. In the archived Qwen experiments, gradient writes make the designated first answer token top-ranked for 132 independently reset targets, comprising 93 new promotions and 39 already top-ranked targets. A separate matched 24-target comparison gives 13 new promotions with Adam versus two with SPSA at equal iteration counts but unequal computational procedures. An 80-row case includes saved continuations and a replay record, while reformulations bound its scope. Six DeepSeek zero-order cases yield one new target-token promotion and one regression. These results support bounded writing feasibility and separate trained expression, question-form behavior, and preservation; first-token rankings do not establish complete-answer success or universal conditions for writable memory.

articles.title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance for TI2I Flow Matching
articles.content: We study Text-and-Image-to-Image (TI2I) flow matching methods for controllable image editing. In a broader generative modeling context, Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is established as a key component responsible for high quality outputs. However, we argue that its role in TI2I modeling is poorly understood. Specifically, we make the surprising observation that the CFG mechanism is implicitly harmful for editing in the noisy phase of flow modeling, hindering instruction following and controllability. We propose a simple correction in the early flow steps, enabling a richer alignment-preservation tradeoff at no extra cost. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated on both pixel-space and latent TI2I flows.

articles.title: When Is Muon Optimal? Radial Fragility and Minimax Geometry
articles.content: Muon replaces a matrix gradient by an approximate polar factor and has shown strong empirical performance in neural-network training. The Isotropic Curvature Model (ICM) provides a curvature-based explanation for this update by asking when gradient orthogonalization minimizes a one-step local-loss surrogate. We investigate the stability of this explanation when the fixed input radius of the ICM is replaced by a general radial law. We introduce the Random-Radius Isotropic Curvature Model (RR-ICM) and the Polar-Factor Admissibility Set, which encodes exact scaled-polar optimality as a geometric condition on the positive polar factor of the gradient. We derive an exact characterization of this set for arbitrary radial laws and show that all nonscalar admissible responses arise from radial atoms aligned with curvature kinks. Consequently, every atomless radial law exhibits zero-capacity rigidity: exact scaled-polar optimality is possible only when the gradient is already a scaled column isometry. To connect the curvature-based framework with the established spectral geometry of Muon, we introduce the Minimax RR-ICM by replacing directional averaging with worst-case optimization over probability laws on the sphere. We prove that every nonzero global minimizer lies on the polar ray of the gradient, while its scale is determined by a one-dimensional convex problem. The corresponding admissibility geometry is a positive-semidefinite trace slab, in sharp contrast to the spherical-zonoid geometry of the RR-ICM. Together, these results expose the radial fragility of average-curvature explanations and provide a new minimax variational characterization of Muon's polar direction.

articles.title: Finite-Time Guarantees for Constrained Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
articles.content: We study reinforcement learning in constrained partially observable Markov decision processes (CPOMDPs), where an agent maximizes reward subject to a cost constraint using only incomplete information about the underlying state. The lack of state observability may require optimal policies to depend on arbitrarily long observation-action histories, making planning and learning challenging. We leverage recent advances in finite-memory approximations of POMDPs and represent finite history windows as states of a constrained MDP. We then develop a primal--dual algorithm that provides the first non-asymptotic guarantees that jointly bound average reward suboptimality and constraint violation in the original CPOMDP. A key challenge is that this finite-window approximation affects both reward values and the set of feasible policies. Under a filter-stability assumption, we derive bounds relating optimality and feasibility in the finite-state model to those in the original CPOMDP, with approximation errors that decay geometrically with the window length. Experiments in partially observable gridworlds demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articles.content:

Abstract: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code. Naturally, this has also led to the development of data science agents that promise automating the design and execution of data science from task formulation to model development. Existing evaluations of agentic data science (agentic DS) assess downstream predictive performance and code correctness, providing preliminary insight in agentic DS capabilities. We argue that these evaluations overlook the fundamental principles of data science: methodological data science- and domain knowledge. articles.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14136v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. articles.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14180v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Organisations that want language-model agents for security work face a choice between open-weight models, which they can run and audit themselves, and far more expensive closed frontier models. We study that choice on CTI-REALM (arXiv:2603.13517), a benchmark in which an agent turns a threat-intelligence report into a working detection by querying a live telemetry store. We evaluate twenty-six models, nineteen open-weight and seven closed, under a common harness, scorer and panel of LLM judges. Our main finding is that an open-weight model can match the strongest closed models at less than a tenth of their cost, provided it is given enough turns. articles.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14186v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Could model-free reinforcement learning algorithms actually be learning a model of the environment? In this work, we apply counterfactual interventions which hold everything about a state fixed, besides a targeted change, to explore if the value function of a Proximal Policy Optimization agent forms a world model of the Crafter environment. Despite only being trained to optimize reward, we discover that the value function learns concepts such as the rules governing when a diamond is collectible, water and food having an impact on health, heuristics regarding inventory, and more. Finally, we discuss the safety implications of our visualizations and some shortcomings of current reinforcement learning agents that will prevent us from building truly advanced machine intelligence.

articles.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14209v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14224v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. articles.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. articles.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14294v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.

Abstract: We propose ConicFlow, which frames constrained sampling from a flow matching model at inference time as an optimal control problem that balances deviation from the pretrained trajectory against reward, subject to hard terminal constraints. We discretize this problem and adapt receding-horizon control, optimizing only a short window of the trajectory at each step for computational tractability. We address the resulting sequence of receding-horizon subproblems with a receding-horizon primal-dual algorithm. Its dual multipliers capture the difficulty of satisfying each constraint and are refined throughout sampling, steering generation toward feasible final samples. We further propose a terminal-estimate variant that avoids accumulating local truncation errors by evaluating the reward and constraints at the predicted terminal point rather than at the end of the current horizon. Abstract: AI-enabled systems must remain dependable when the conditions under which they operate change (e.g., due to input perturbations, distribution shifts, or changes in external dependencies). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14360v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) alignment often assumes that the user interacting with a model is also the primary beneficiary of its behavior. Yet in many consequential settings, one person directs the system while another bears the consequences. We study this problem in caregiver-mediated healthcare, where parents, pet owners, and caregivers make decisions for children, animals, and older adults. We introduce an evidence-grounded benchmark spanning veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care, and test whether AI advisors maintain appropriate care when users express clinically inferior preferences. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14381v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as scientific assistants, yet we still lack reliable ways to evaluate whether they can investigate a system rather than merely answer a prompt. A useful evaluation must let agents choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make causal decisions, while keeping the environment coherent across repeated observations and interventions and preserving objective ground truth. We introduce ACED-BENCH (Active Causal Evidence and Decision Benchmark), a neuro-symbolic benchmark built around this requirement. The key idea is to separate the readable scientific surface from the formal causal world: LLMs generate natural-language scenarios and task text, while hidden probabilistic graphical models define the causal graph, data-generating process, intervention semantics, validation checks, and oracle answers. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14389v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Benchmark scores tell us what an LLM can do, but not how much energy is required to deliver that capability. We directly measure this trade-off for 86 open-weight model checkpoints, evaluated on seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms ranging from a consumer GPU to an eight-GPU server. We find large differences in energy efficiency even among models with similar capability. Most configurations lie away from the score--energy Pareto frontier: they use a median of 2.6--4.8$\times$ more energy than another configuration that scores at least as well, with differences reaching 27$\times$. Reasoning can improve capability, but enabling thinking increases energy by about 3.7$\times$ on average, and the benefit depends strongly on the model family and output budget. Abstract: High-throughput perturbation screens increasingly use machine-learning models to predict the effects of gene combinations that were never measured. Abstract: We study online task assignment with reusable resources. This problem arises in peer reviewer assignment, skill-based call routing, rideshare matching, emergency dispatch, and crowdsourcing: Tasks arrive according to a geometric process and must be immediately assigned to servers that become temporarily busy, yielding rewards that depend on the task-server pair. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19042v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding the mechanism behind why diffusion models memorize their training data remains an open question in generative modeling. In this paper, we examine this question from two perspectives: (a) the model-level perspective concerning the onset of memorization in a model during training, and (b) the sample-level perspective concerning the proclivity of an individual sample to be memorized by a given model. We show that the so-called input loss curvature, or the Frobenius norm of the Hessian of the diffusion model's training loss, is an effective metric for quantifying both perspectives on memorization. In particular, we empirically demonstrate that input curvatures averaged across training and validation samples can identify when a model is likely to start regurgitating its training data when tracked over training time. We study Particle Polynomial Relaxation (PPR), a moment-based nonconvex continuous reformulation possessing an advantageous optimization landscape. An extended variant with discrete local-search refinement reaches the published optimum on all sixty Biq Mac instances evaluated by a recent neural branch-and-bound method. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Information-theoretic exploration is of primary interest in methodological studies of reinforcement learning (RL) and computational cognitive neuroscience, while the established RL theory builds regret guarantees on confidence sets. This situation leaves open the conditions under which the information-driven exploration found in nature is more advantageous than the exploration of the established RL theory. We put the state-of-the-art methods of these two paradigms, Active Inference (AIF) and Bayes-UCBVI, on an equal footing: both act through the same state abstraction of a tabular MDP with $S$ states, and their greedy forms differ only in the exploration term. We find that AIF's information gain decays too fast to serve as a confidence width, locking greedy agents that explore by it out of the optimal action. arXiv:2610.19053v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Inference of phylogenetic trees from sequences plays a central role in understanding evolutionary relationships, with applications ranging from tracking pathogen spread to reconstructing the history of life. Conventionally, practitioners obtain posteriors over trees using likelihood-based methods like MCMC. However, likelihoods are only available for simple evolutionary models with restrictive assumptions. For realistic evolutionary models, inference using conventional methods is prohibitively expensive, inaccurate, or even impossible. In practice, practitioners settle for using as flexible a conventional method as possible, even though they expect it is misspecified. In principle, we could use simulation-based inference: simulate tree and sequence data from an evolutionary model and train a neural network to predict the posterior over trees given sequences. Abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) across geographically distributed and poorly interconnected compute pools or data centers has become a topic of significant interest. However, a central challenge remains: it is well known that increasing the number of model replicas (replica scaling) while fixing the total training budget leads to monotonically decreasing performance. Abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification remains an important challenge in AI. Hierarchical Bayesian methods provide a principled framework for this by representing unknown quantities through posterior distributions. Joint inference of neural-network parameters and prior hyperparameters is challenging for conventional Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods due to strong dependencies. Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the reasoning of autoregressive and discrete-diffusion language models. Language models that generate continuous token embeddings are emerging as a strong alternative, but RL post-training for them remains understudied. We propose \method{}, a post-training framework for continuous flow language models. Such a model denoises token embeddings over multiple steps and decodes them into discrete tokens only at the last step. To obtain pathwise gradients, which backpropagate through continuous actions and have much lower variance than REINFORCE, we introduce a critic that estimates the value of intermediate token embeddings, bypassing the non-differentiable decoding step. Abstract: Voice agents built on large language models (LLMs) now handle customer calls, but in regulated applications completing the task is not enough: the agent must follow a conversational flow set by law. In debt collection, it must confirm it is speaking to the debtor before mentioning the debt, identify itself and the creditor, state the amount, and avoid prohibited language. Every creditor turns these rules into its own procedure and revises it. We ask whether a small, self-hosted policy can be trained once and then follow regulated procedures it has never seen. One machine-readable specification per deployment, FlowSpec, generates the policy instruction, gates the tools, supplies the supervision and defines the tests; the agent speaks only approved catalogue sentences. Abstract: Abstractive summarization remains challenging across languages, where linguistic quality and factual consistency may diverge, particularly in low-resource settings. We present a standardized zero-shot benchmark of eight closed-source and open-weight LLMs on size-matched English and Bengali XL-Sum test sets. Our evaluation combines lexical and semantic metrics with reference-free factuality verification and multidimensional LLM-as-a-Judge assessment, providing a comprehensive analysis of both surface-level quality and factual reliability in multilingual summarization. articles.title: Can LLMs Access their World Knowledge for Event Prediction?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19021v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work has questioned whether large language models (LLMs) can be useful for temporal event prediction. Despite vast pretrained world knowledge, LLMs often underperform simpler specialized models. We ask whether this knowledge is truly inaccessible, or whether current methods fail to present event prediction in a form LLMs can use. We argue for the latter and show that LLMs become effective event forecasters when the interface is designed around two choices. The first grounds each event in a natural-language description, and the second separates event semantics from the prediction space to prevent semantic bias from label associations. To test this, we introduce DescribeEvent, a benchmark of ~150K events across seven datasets and six domains with event-level descriptions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19026v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse attention reduces the KV-cache traffic that dominates long-context LLM decoding, but practical methods largely operate at coarse granularity. Token-level selection offers finer control, yet presents two challenges: low-dimensional scoring may lose query--key structure needed for accurate ranking, while gathering scattered selected tokens can offset the resulting latency benefit. We introduce Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA) to address both challenges. For selection quality, JSSA learns a shared low-dimensional query--key subspace by minimizing token-score preservation error. We upper-bound the resulting non-convex objective with a tractable marginal objective that admits a closed-form spectral solution; direct refinement of the exact objective provides no measurable improvement in the tested settings. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19028v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Science fiction is widely credited with unsettling gender. This article asks whether that holds at the linguistic level, in how readily gendered reference gives way to its counterpart, a neutral term, or other social category, and whether it separates the genre from general fiction. It does so by masking man/men, woman/women, and person/people across same-period science fiction and general fiction corpora and classifying RoBERTa's five likeliest substitutes by gender. Retention and displacement are permutation-tested over five resampling rounds, and the underlying sentences are read closely. Both corpora cross the gender binary in both directions, but unequally: where woman is masked, the model predicts a masculine term about twice as often as it predicts a feminine term where man is masked. Abstract: Record linkage and demographic inference from names are routine demands in social science. Most approaches to these problems require labeled training data that are difficult or costly to acquire. For ethnicity inference from names, I show that large language models (LLMs) achieve up to 83.8% accuracy on U.S. voter files, compared to 78.0% for name-supplemented BISG. Abstract: Chatbot Arena ranks language models with the Bradley-Terry model, which gives each model one score and so assumes Luce's choice axiom. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) allows language models to adapt their behavior from instructions and demonstrations in a prompt, but accuracy alone does not reveal how contextual information controls their predictions. We study the acquisition and trainability of ICL with a controlled diagnostic that separates copying a nearby demonstration from integrating information across the prompt. Across 17 models, about a third prefer the copied answer, a few are undecided, and the rest prefer the rule-consistent answer, which goes with higher accuracy and with control by the requested value rather than the closest conflicting example. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emerging decision models such as JEV provide typed interfaces that map task instructions and observations directly to choices, judgments, and scores. As these models are increasingly used for automated decision-making, understanding their reliability under adversarial manipulation becomes critical. We introduce DecisionRobust, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of decision models across textual and visual inputs. Our benchmark covers practical decision-making scenarios and a diverse suite of attacks, including semantics-preserving text perturbations, image perturbations, and prompt injection in both modalities. We curate evaluation sets through external validity checks and cross-model candidate selection. We evaluate 30 model configurations on text tasks and 17 on vision tasks, including 24 and 12 held-out models, respectively, that are excluded from candidate selection. Our experiments reveal several key findings.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Feature distillation is usually expected to add to logit distillation. We find that this expectation does not hold for two common feature losses in compact multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), and analyze why through their gradients. The gradient of a projection-based loss is orthogonal to the task gradient, while that of Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), a similarity-based loss, is weakly aligned with it. CKA lowers the word error rate (WER) on non-English languages, but at the expense of data-rich English. Three loss-level remedies (one trained, two probed) all fall short, and the CKA gradient overlaps with the subspace English uses in the shared encoder by 97.5% to 99.5% (about 81% by chance). Guided by this diagnosis, we propose CAFE (Confined-Adapter Feature distillation), which confines the CKA gradient to adapters that English bypasses, addressing the trade-off in the parameters rather than in the loss.
